title: Team Agreement
concept: A way to face outside pressure together. When family, friends or strangers lean on you as a couple, it’s coming at you both: not a flaw in either of you or in the relationship.
whenToUse: When disapproval or discrimination from outside (a relative, a friend, a stranger, a colleague) follows you home and starts turning into a fight between the two of you. If the pressure comes from your partner, this isn’t the tool: if they check, restrict or punish your contact with others, stop and use the Help Lines; otherwise use the Green Rule.
steps: Believe first. The partner who is told says: “I believe you, and I’m not going to explain it away.” Then ask whether they need to vent, be comforted or act.
Pause before reacting. Don’t act on the comment or the look in the moment.
Trace the source: is this about the two of you, or about them? Say “That’s coming from them, not from us,” then ask what each of you needs.
Name the unit out loud: “We’re on the same side of this.”
Agree your response, together, for next time. Decide how the two of you respond, never how much contact your partner has with their own family, friends, money, phone or movements.

phrases.text: That’s coming from them, not from us.
We’re on the same side of this.
Same team. The problem is the problem.

working: The same dig comes at every family dinner, aimed at B. On the drive home A says, “That’s coming from them, not from us,” asks what B needs, and they agree how to answer it next time.
notWorking: Back home, A asks B, “Well, did your mum have a point?” Now they’re arguing about her comment instead of facing it together.
activity: Each of you names one recurring outside pressure. Practise saying “We’re on the same side of this.” Agree one thing you’ll do differently next time, and write it down.
warn: Whether to be out is each person’s own decision. No agreement can require either of you to hide who you are or to be outed. If the pressure comes from your partner, this isn’t outside pressure: use the Green Rule, and the Help Lines if you’re afraid.
note: Restart line for when you catch yourself blaming: “Same team. The problem is the problem.” Swap “You always do this” for “This pattern keeps coming up for us.” Never use it as a muzzle (“Same team, so stop complaining”).
